title: The generalization of shared reality: When communication about one target shapes evaluations of other targets
rationale_A: Two experiments vary audience-commonality and recall conditions and measure evaluations of described social targets.
rationale_B: Two message-tuning experiments assess evaluations, but the abstract does not specify the stimuli or whether the interaction is an eligible survey-content procedure.

title: A Design and a Model for Investigating the Heterogeneity of Context Effects in Public Opinion Surveys
rationale_A: A methodological demonstration mentions framing effects without establishing whether a new eligible experiment was conducted.
rationale_B: A reported framing-treatment application evaluates survey context effects on US education judgments, but data origin and presentation modality are unstated.

title: Is voice really persuasive? The influence of modality in virtual assistant interactions and two alternative explanations
rationale_A: An online experiment compares text and voice virtual assistants and measures brand attitudes and purchase intentions.
rationale_B: The online study compares assistant modalities and persuasion outcomes, but does not establish whether participants receive fixed content or interact adaptively.

title: Types of HPV Vaccine Misinformation Circulating on Twitter (X) That Parents Find Most Concerning: Insights From a Cross-Sectional Survey and Content Analysis
rationale_A: US parents receive randomly selected misinformation tweets and choose those they find most concerning.
rationale_B: Parents judge randomly sampled existing tweets, but the account does not establish whether item sampling constitutes an experimental content contrast beyond descriptive rating.
